title: Laws of Reflection
subject: Physics
objective: To hit a hidden target with a laser and a mirror you need 2 rules: i = r (both measured from the normal) and all three rays in one plane.

fill.q: First law: angle of incidence = angle of ____.
Angles are measured from the ____, not from the surface.
The incident ray, normal and reflected ray lie in the same ____.
A ray along the normal returns along ____.

tf.q: i = r for every reflection at a mirror.
The angle of incidence is measured from the mirror surface.
tf.explain: It is measured from the normal.

tf.q: A ray hitting a mirror at 90° to the surface reflects back on itself.
The reflected ray can leave the plane of incidence.
tf.explain: Second law: all three lie in one plane.

ar.a: A ray falling along the normal retraces its path.
ar.explain: The first law gives r = i = 0.

ar.a: Angle of incidence is measured from the mirror surface.
ar.r: The normal is perpendicular to the mirror.
ar.explain: A is false (measured from the normal); R is true.

mcq.q: A ray makes 30° with the mirror surface. Angle of reflection:
If i = 45°, the angle between incident and reflected rays is:

options: perpendicular to the mirror at the point of incidence

mcq.q: Which law says the three rays lie in one plane?

num.q: A ray strikes a plane mirror at 35° to the surface. Find the angle of incidence, angle of reflection and the angle between incident and reflected rays.
steps: Angle between the rays = i + r = 110°

num.q: The angle between the incident and reflected rays is 70°. Find the angle of incidence and the angle the ray makes with the mirror.
steps: i + r = 70° and i = r, so i = 35°

short.q: State the two laws of reflection.
short.solution: 1. The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. 2. The incident ray, the normal at the point of incidence and the reflected ray lie in the same plane.

short.q: A ray strikes a mirror at 25° to the surface. Find i and r.
